item.text:
**6B.3 Assessment**
Mostly no. There is real but narrow evidence of targeted support for vulnerable populations, especially Rohingya/host communities and some women-focused humanitarian services. But the broader 2024 record points the other way: repression, unequal protection, and worsening security and discrimination for minorities and other vulnerable groups.

**Accepted Claims**
- [World Bank Helps Bangladesh Provide Basic Services, Opportunities, and Build Resilience for Displaced Rohingya and Host Communities](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co) | World Bank | May 28, 2024 | Claim: Bangladesh and partners funded health, nutrition, education, water, shelters, livelihood support, and GBV prevention for Rohingya and host communities. This is the strongest positive evidence that Hasina’s state did prioritize vulnerable groups in at least one major humanitarian track. | QIDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- [UNICEF and Japan join hands to improve the well-being of Bangladeshi and Rohingya children living in Cox’s Bazar and Bhasan Char](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/262180-unicef-and-japan-join-hands-improve-the-well-being-of-bangladeshi-and-rohingya-children-living) | United Nations in Bangladesh | March 3, 2024 | Claim: UNICEF reported expanded services for Rohingya children, women, and host communities, including education, WASH, health, and nutrition. Positive, but this is humanitarian delivery rather than proof of a broad state priority under Hasina. | QIDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 5B.8

- [UNFPA Bangladesh Annual Report 2024](https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/unfpa-bangladesh-annual-report-2024) | UNFPA Bangladesh | 2024 | Claim: UNFPA delivered targeted services to women, girls, indigenous communities, transgender people, sex workers, and disaster-affected areas, including reproductive health and cash assistance. This is concrete inclusion evidence, though it is partner-led and not strong proof of Hasina’s own prioritization. | QIDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- [Bangladesh - Cash Transfer Modernization Project: Improving Transparency and Efficiency of Safety Nets](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099739201032424234) | World Bank | January 1, 2024 | Claim: Bangladesh already had cash-transfer programs aimed at the poorest and most socially excluded, including widows, older people, and disabled people. This is limited positive background for prioritizing vulnerable groups, but it also shows the system still needed modernization. | QIDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 5B.8

- [Bangladesh: Türk decries government crackdown, urges respect for international human rights standards](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) | United Nations / OHCHR | July 26, 2024 | Claim: more than 170 people were reported killed, some injured people were denied medical care, and the UN said there was no effort to protect people from attacks by groups affiliated with the government. This is strong negative evidence against prioritizing vulnerable civilians. | QIDs: 6B.3, 6B.1, 5B.7

- [Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Claim: minorities and refugees, especially Rohingya, faced discrimination and insecure access to health care, employment, and education, alongside punitive camp policies and broad corruption. This is direct evidence against equitable prioritization of vulnerable groups. | QIDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- [Bangladesh: Repression, Security Force Abuses Discredit Elections](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections) | Human Rights Watch | January 11, 2024 | Claim: authorities arrested critics and used repression and violence before the election. While not a service-delivery item, it shows the regime was prioritizing control over the safety and access needs of vulnerable political opponents and civil society. | QIDs: 6B.3, 6B.1, 5B.1

- [Fears grip ethnic minorities after deadly violence in Bangladesh](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/fears-grip-ethnic-minorities-after-deadly-violence-in-bangladesh-3626672) | Reuters | September 21, 2024 | Claim: ethnic minorities in the Chittagong Hill Tracts were living in fear after clashes, with homes and businesses burned and families displaced despite heavy patrols. This is direct evidence that poor regions and minorities were not securely protected. | QIDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1

**Search Gap**
- I found strong evidence for targeted humanitarian support, but it is mostly partner-led and narrow.
- I did not find convincing evidence that Hasina’s 2024 governing strategy broadly prioritized vulnerable groups across the whole country.
- The negative evidence is stronger on minorities, Rohingya, and crisis protection than the positive evidence is on inclusive state prioritization.
